newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call money falls on Central Bank move.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call money falls on Central Bank move.

text.p: The Philippine overnight money fell to 10.3125 percent on Monday following the 25 basis point reduction of Central Bank's benchmark rate to 10.25 percent
The average call loan rate was at 10.53125 percent last Friday.
"The banks just adjusted their rates slightly above the Central Bank rate. The market is very liquid anyway," one trader said.
Turnover was moderate at 25.951 billion pesos with done rates ranging from 10.28125 to 11.28125 percent.

Banks were long on the pesos in the past two trading days after the Central Bank closed its termed reverse repo windows. It reopened the windows early on Monday but attached some terms which made banks hesitate to buy.
Buying parties are now told to pay the necessary income tax upfront instead of by the end of the year.
Buyers, both banks and individual investors, were told to waive the secrecy of their deposits, allowing the internal revenue agency to monitor secondary trading of reverse repos.
The finance department had complained that banks were not paying the right amount of interest income tax since secondary transactions are difficult to track.
"The additional terms have discouraged many banks from buying ... since they don't know how their clients will react to the new provisions," one trader said.

Banks were forced to invest their excess funds in government securities, depressing further the secondary Treasury bill rates, which went down 40 basis points from the average rates posted last week. Traders were expecting the same sharp decline in this week's auction. - RAMONCITO DELA CRUZ 63 2 8418938
